names.legendary: Old Bootsworth, Walker of the Lost Roads

lore.common: Hides its partner every morning, usually under the bed, sometimes in another county.
lore.uncommon: Always picks the deepest puddle. It insists this is a perfectly sensible shortcut.
lore.rare: Leaves muddy footprints that keep walking after the boot stops. They have already explored the attic.
lore.epic: Stamped once on the football field and every puddle in town leapt from its hole. The referee called off the match for weather manipulation.
lore.legendary: Left behind at a campsite, Bootsworth walked a thousand miles home by itself. It kicked its owner, wiped its feet and demanded fresh socks.

names.legendary: Velouria, Queen of the Last Dance

lore.common: Insists on spinning whenever somebody carries a full glass.
lore.uncommon: Hooks its hem onto furniture just to delay important departures.
lore.rare: Grows hidden pockets large enough for a hamster and a week's worth of secrets.
lore.epic: Spun through the royal ball so fiercely that every chandelier joined the waltz. The orchestra was last seen dancing on the ceiling.
lore.legendary: Velouria danced with the midnight wind until the clocks refused to strike twelve. Her silk still carries the last song that kept a thousand guests from growing old.

names.legendary: Lord Balaclavor, Faceless of the Peaks

lore.common: Makes your nose itch the instant both hands are busy. It feeds on the resulting frustration.
lore.uncommon: Has three eyeholes, and not one of them is where your eyes are. Insists this is fashion.
lore.rare: Knits new openings whenever you sneeze, then charges you for the alterations.
lore.epic: Pulled itself over an entire ski resort. Nobody could recognise anyone, and the mayor spent two days arresting his own reflection.
lore.legendary: At the summit of the oldest mountain, Balaclavor wears the blizzard like a hood. Even winter must ask permission to see his face.

names.legendary: Red Jack, the Thousand-Knot Renegade

lore.common: Ties itself around the wrong end of the dog's neck. The dog is now a cowboy.
lore.uncommon: Makes anyone wearing it feel like a fearless outlaw, right up until Mum calls them in.
lore.rare: Whips itself over the face of every sneezer nearby. The library looks like a very polite gang.
lore.epic: Lassoed a stampede with one flying corner. The cattle agreed to return if it stopped behaving like a sheriff.
lore.legendary: Every wind on the prairie owes Red Jack a favour. He wears no face beneath the cloth, just the sound of distant hoofbeats.

names.legendary: Capitanna, Mistress of the Silent Swim

lore.common: Pulls every strand of hair at once when removed. Says it is improving your posture.
lore.uncommon: Clamps over both ears until the pool sounds like a very distant argument.
lore.rare: Squeaks beneath the water like a dolphin. The lifeguard has checked the pool for wildlife three times.
lore.epic: Stretched across an Olympic pool and turned the whole surface into a giant trampoline. The divers were delighted.
lore.legendary: The first swim cap to cross the seven seas alone. Captains still salute the tiny rubber crown floating beyond the horizon.

names.legendary: Lord Busby, the Unmoving Sentinel

lore.common: Tickles every royal guard's nose during inspection. The sneeze penalty is severe.
lore.uncommon: Grows so tall on a guard's head that doorways become sworn enemies.
lore.rare: Lets out a tiny bear growl when tourists make silly faces. They stop immediately.
lore.epic: Stood guard at the palace gate for three centuries without moving. The uniforms changed; the enormous hat refused.
lore.legendary: An ancient black-furred crown that never bows, not even to kings. Legends claim it is the palace's true commander and the soldiers are merely its legs.

names.legendary: Beraine, Muse of the Crooked Crown

lore.common: Slides over one ear every morning. Says symmetry is for amateurs.
lore.uncommon: Makes its wearer believe they are an undiscovered genius. The sketchbook disagrees.
lore.rare: Draws little moustaches on every portrait in the museum, including the portraits already wearing moustaches.
lore.epic: Tilted dramatically during a poetry reading and pulled the entire cafe sideways. The croissants escaped down the street.
lore.legendary: Painted a sunset so magnificent the real Sun came down for lessons. The stars still ask her to autograph their reflections.

names.legendary: Sir Bowlington, Minister of Hats

lore.common: Rolls down the street every time its owner performs a dramatic bow.
lore.uncommon: Insists on being paired with an umbrella. Has rejected seventeen perfectly decent raincoats.
lore.rare: Tips itself to every passer-by, including lamp posts. Its owner has been late to work for a decade.
lore.epic: Called every gentleman's hat in town into one whirling airborne parliament. They passed a motion abolishing bad hair days.
lore.legendary: Bowlington once ran a whole railway station after its manager went missing. Every train arrived punctually, although all passengers were required to wear a hat.

names.legendary: Lord Puddlebrim, Crown of the Downpour

lore.common: Drops over its wearer's eyes just when someone says LOOK OVER THERE.
lore.uncommon: Sends every drop of rain around its rim and directly onto a neighbour.
lore.rare: Stores an entire puddle in its brim. Laugh at it once and discover where the water goes.
lore.epic: Turned upside down at a music festival and collected enough mud to build a second stage. The headliner performed from the hat.
lore.legendary: Puddlebrim caught the first rain of the monsoon and wore it like a crown. Ducks still migrate to the little lake that forms over his forehead.

names.legendary: Regaliax, Crown of the Unworthy

lore.common: Slides down over the king's eyes every time he makes a speech.
lore.uncommon: Makes its wearer announce nonsense laws, including mandatory pudding on Thursdays.
lore.rare: Chooses a random peasant to be king for a day. The actual king finds this educational.
lore.epic: Rolled away from the coronation, crowned the palace goat and started a constitutional crisis.
lore.legendary: Has crowned emperors, prophets and exactly one very confused cat. Regaliax answers only to whoever can resist giving orders once it's on their head.

names.legendary: Mufflethra, Queen of the Quiet Storm

lore.common: Makes everyone answer questions that nobody asked.
lore.uncommon: Gets so cozy in winter that it refuses to come off at bedtime.
lore.rare: Can silence a brass band for exactly ten seconds. The band practices faster to compensate.
lore.epic: Swallowed the entire roar of a packed stadium during a championship. The referee heard one lonely person eating crisps.
lore.legendary: Mufflethra rests upon the frozen summit where thunder first learned silence. When she closes her velvet ears, even blizzards tiptoe past.

names.legendary: Inspector Fedorius of the Missing Moon

lore.common: Tips its brim at strangers and accidentally hides the wearer's eyes.
lore.uncommon: Convinces its owner they are in a detective film. The mystery is always the missing keys.
lore.rare: Can smell a secret through three closed doors, but never finds out which one opens.
lore.epic: Pulled its brim down over the whole city and turned noon into a black-and-white detective film. The pigeons began narrating their own crimes.
lore.legendary: Fedorius solved the mystery of the stolen moon by following a trail of silver hat pins. The moon had merely borrowed a coat and gone undercover at the theatre.

names.legendary: Topperon, Crown of the Four Winds

lore.common: Blows off a perfectly still head whenever somebody says lovely weather.
lore.uncommon: Gives its wearer the appearance of knowing secrets. The wearer knows absolutely none.
lore.rare: Leaps from head to head at a party, changing each guest's accent along with their outfit.
lore.epic: Pulled a hundred rabbits from its own brim during a magic show. The magician is now employed by the rabbits.
lore.legendary: Topperon chooses a different ruler every century, landing on the head of whoever most needs courage. Once it chose a donkey, and the kingdom enjoyed an unusually peaceful reign.

names.legendary: Bandora, Keeper of the Unbroken Focus

lore.common: Slides over the eyes exactly when someone prepares to catch a ball.
lore.uncommon: Keeps sweat out of a runner's eyes, then squeezes it out onto their nose at the finish.
lore.rare: Can hold back a hurricane of hair without shifting a millimetre. The hairstyle thanks it quietly.
lore.epic: Snapped loose at the athletics final and launched every competitor's hair into matching vertical spikes. They finished looking like a forest of hedgehogs.
lore.legendary: Bandora was worn by the first champion to cross the desert without turning aside. Its woven threads still guide lost travellers toward the finish, even after the race is over.

names.legendary: Doctor Quadsworth of Cloud College

lore.common: Swings its tassel into the graduate's nose just as the camera flashes.
lore.uncommon: Falls off whenever somebody bends to pick up their diploma. Calls this an academic experiment.
lore.rare: Collects forgotten degrees and awards them to exceptionally clever pigeons.
lore.epic: Launched itself into the sky with a thousand graduation caps and formed a flying university. The lecturers now commute by kite.
lore.legendary: Doctor Quadsworth sailed through seven kingdoms on an endless graduation breeze, granting degrees to scholars who could answer one question: where did the hat land?

names.legendary: Lady Drylocks, the Unsoaked Sovereign

lore.common: Makes enough crinkling noise to drown out an entire shower concert.
lore.uncommon: Inflates into a ridiculous balloon whenever its owner sings a high note.
lore.rare: Repels not only water but every stray splash in the bathroom, including the dog's bath.
lore.epic: Expanded into a waterproof dome over the hotel swimming pool. The swimmers demanded a refund when it began raining inside the hotel instead.
lore.legendary: Lady Drylocks once walked beneath a waterfall that fell from the clouds all the way to the ocean floor. Her hair stayed perfectly styled; the waterfall needed a week to recover its dignity.

names.legendary: Maskara, the Breath Beneath the Ice

lore.common: Freezes stiff from its owner's breath before the chairlift reaches the top.
lore.uncommon: Makes everybody on the ski bus look like members of the world's least threatening ninja clan.
lore.rare: Traps a warm pocket of mountain air around its wearer even when the wind steals everyone else's hats.
lore.epic: Took one deep breath on the slope and blew enough warm fog to hide the ski school from the instructor. The lift operator went looking with a bell.
lore.legendary: Maskara sheltered the faces of a hundred travellers through a winter without dawn. Each morning her wool still held a trace of warmth from the fire they left behind.

names.legendary: Lady Solshade, Mistress of Midday

lore.common: Flies off the moment someone says the beach is not windy.
lore.uncommon: Has a brim so wide it accidentally steals shade from strangers.
lore.rare: Drags its wearer around the garden in pursuit of a sunbeam that is always moving.
lore.epic: Unfurled a brim large enough to shade an entire seaside carnival; the sunbathers formed a protest committee.
lore.legendary: Lady Solshade once sheltered a desert caravan beneath a single brim for seven scorching days. The sun sent a formal complaint about unfair competition.

names.legendary: Tiariella, Empress of the Unchosen

lore.common: Falls into the punch bowl just as the photographer says smile.
lore.uncommon: Sparkles so fiercely that even the chandeliers feel underdressed.
lore.rare: Makes whoever wears it speak with royal dignity, including when ordering chips at the beach.
lore.epic: Crowned every guest at the ballroom gala, then made the chandelier bow to an elderly pigeon wearing a pearl necklace.
lore.legendary: Tiariella crowns those who show kindness when no one watches. The richest queens have sought her jewels for centuries; she still prefers the children who share their toys.

names.legendary: Visora, the Umpire of Noon

lore.common: Protects your eyes while leaving the top of your head to negotiate with the sun.
lore.uncommon: Throws a sulk whenever its brim gets turned backwards.
lore.rare: Tilts itself to deflect glare from a tennis serve at the perfect moment.
lore.epic: Cast such a wide shadow over centre court that the grass decided it was nighttime and went to sleep. The final moved to the car park.
lore.legendary: Called every line correctly in a match that lasted three summers. The ball never landed outside its shadow, and the human umpire opened a bakery.

names.legendary: Madame Tressoria of the Lost Applause

lore.common: Wobbles on its owner's head whenever the music starts.
lore.uncommon: Grows one rebellious curl that refuses to join the rest.
lore.rare: Changes its hairstyle overnight to suit the next day's weather.
lore.epic: Expanded into an enormous tower of curls during the closing scene of the play. The actors needed a map to find the curtain.
lore.legendary: Performed every role in a legendary theatre without ever changing its wearer. Each strand remembers a character, and the audience still hears applause when it is brushed.

names.legendary: Helmorian, the Unbroken Crown

lore.common: Squashes every hairstyle into a pancake and calls it a safety upgrade.
lore.uncommon: Bumps doorframes with the confidence of someone who believes the building should move instead.
lore.rare: Protects a rider from a spectacular fall, then proudly displays its dents like battle medals.
lore.epic: Stopped a runaway parade float when it rolled beneath the wheel. The crowd gave the dented helmet a standing ovation.
lore.legendary: Helmorian guarded the head of an ancient mountain messenger through seven landslides. The messenger carried peace between rival villages, and every scratch on the helm became part of the treaty.

names.legendary: The Overcoat with a Kingdom Inside

lore.common: Hides the house keys in the one pocket you have never used.
lore.uncommon: Jams its zipper halfway up and laughs while you try to escape.
lore.rare: Walks to school by itself whenever its owner forgets it on the hook. Its grades are excellent.
lore.epic: Raised its collar so high it hid the entire office from view. The employees went home early because nobody could find the manager.
lore.legendary: Its oldest inside pocket contains a miniature kingdom with its own seasons. The queen has asked the tailor for another lining because the winters are getting cold.

names.legendary: Old Denim Dan, the Walking Wardrobe

lore.common: Comes out of the wash slightly smaller and swears the wearer is growing.
lore.uncommon: Hoards old receipts and sweet wrappers in pockets that haven't been emptied since spring.
lore.rare: Rips its own knee into fashionable shapes whenever somebody mentions dress codes.
lore.epic: Turned the whole laundry blue and then marched through town spreading its new denim colour scheme. Even the mayor's dog matched.
lore.legendary: Denim Dan walked away from his owner after a century without a wash and opened a tailor's shop. Every pair he stitches has a pocket leading somewhere mysterious.

names.legendary: Granny Longstitch, Who Wrapped Winter

lore.common: Gets caught in the car door and spends the journey admiring the road.
lore.uncommon: Dries the dog's paws and your face using the same suspicious corner.
lore.rare: Wraps itself protectively around anybody who says they are cold, including a rather surprised snowman.
lore.epic: Absorbed the entire paddling pool during a beach picnic, then wrung out a wave that carried the sandcastle away.
lore.legendary: Granny Longstitch knitted a scarf long enough to wrap an entire winter. The snow stopped falling inside its loops, and the town enjoyed spring one month early.

names.legendary: Magistrix, Robe of a Thousand Minds

lore.common: Flaps its huge sleeves whenever its owner talks, and the pigeons outside flap back.
lore.uncommon: Hides examination answers beneath its hem. Unfortunately, every answer is "perhaps".
lore.rare: Billowed out so dramatically on the stage that the professor nearly floated away.
lore.epic: Unfurled its sleeves at graduation and carried the entire faculty into the clouds. The ceremony continued over video call.
lore.legendary: Has worn so many professors that it now gives the lectures itself. Nobody noticed, except that the jokes got better.

names.legendary: Sir Bibbington, Shield of the Highchair

lore.common: Stops one spoonful of puree and lets six land on the floor. Claims the numbers are respectable.
lore.uncommon: Unties itself just before dessert, a strategic retreat known only to baby clothing.
lore.rare: Catches flying food and fires it back at the spoon. The highchair remains undefeated.
lore.epic: Spread its little fabric wings across the banquet hall and caught a spaghetti tornado before it touched a single guest.
lore.legendary: Saved an entire kingdom from the Great Porridge Flood with one enormous pocket. The royal hounds have never forgiven its efficiency.

names.legendary: Madame Liftoria, Queen of Twin Moons

lore.common: Entangles every sock in the washing machine and calls the result modern art.
lore.uncommon: Has seventeen tiny hooks. Not one agrees to cooperate when its owner is in a hurry.
lore.rare: Escaped the clothesline and caught a passing kite by its tail. Both refused to land.
lore.epic: Opened its straps in a gale and sailed across the county like a two-masted pirate ship. The coastguard filed an unusually detailed report.
lore.legendary: Liftoria once held two falling moons in her enchanted cups until the dawn. The celestial council still argues whether the support was structural or emotional.

names.legendary: Sir Steelheart, the Dragon's Last Regret

lore.common: Clanks on every step. Sneaking up on people is an abandoned career.
lore.uncommon: Gets so hot in the summer sun that a knight once cooked breakfast on it.
lore.rare: Bounces arrows back at whoever fired them. Archers now shoot apology notes instead.
lore.epic: Deflected a dragon's fiery sneeze straight into the clouds. The sky smelled of toasted marshmallows for a week.
lore.legendary: For centuries Steelheart has guarded the heart of a knight whose name was lost. Dragons pass down a warning about the one breastplate that once made their king apologise.

names.legendary: Mailgorath, Armour of the Last Oath

lore.common: Announces every step with a jingle. Nobody has successfully sneaked into a castle wearing it.
lore.uncommon: Collects crumbs between its rings. A knight could live off one banquet's leftovers for weeks.
lore.rare: Links its iron rings together so tightly that arrows bounce away to ask for directions.
lore.epic: Shook itself after a rainy joust and sprayed an entire banquet with water. The king ordered a second moat for the dining hall.
lore.legendary: Mailgorath is woven from a million vows of protection. No sword has pierced its rings, though it has defeated more knights by being too heavy to stand in.

names.legendary: Cuirassus, Shield of the Last Dawn

lore.common: Makes knights bow awkwardly to reach their soup.
lore.uncommon: Reflects an opponent's intimidating face back at them, twice as nervous.
lore.rare: Deflects arrows, insults and a poorly aimed wedding bouquet.
lore.epic: Turned aside the entire siege of a hilltop fortress. The defenders spent the afternoon polishing its chest instead of fighting.
lore.legendary: Was forged in the first sunrise to protect the last defender of a forgotten city. Its surface still carries every sunrise that city never got to see.

names.legendary: Dryadonna, Guardian of Tiny Disasters

lore.common: Opens one sticky tab during the least convenient supermarket queue.
lore.uncommon: Crackles with every crawling step like a secret mission going badly.
lore.rare: Holds a suspicious amount of liquid while maintaining an expression of complete innocence.
lore.epic: Saved an entire nursery from a catastrophic juice-box spill. The adults awarded it a medal and immediately changed it.
lore.legendary: Legend says Dryadonna kept a royal baby dry through forty days of rain while the palace roof leaked. The grateful king named a fountain after it, which felt unkind.

names.legendary: Lady Mailloria of the Endless Lanes

lore.common: Twists its shoulder straps on the first dive and acts as though that was the plan.
lore.uncommon: Stretches around the whole family, but chooses a different awkward fit for each swimmer.
lore.rare: Pulls its wearer through the pool like a tiny secret motor. The lifeguard keeps checking for flippers.
lore.epic: Stretched across the competition pool and turned the final lap into a trampoline race. The medals were awarded for style.
lore.legendary: Lady Mailloria swam through the midnight sea wearing a thousand stolen moonbeams. Her wake still glitters in the lanes of every abandoned lido.

names.legendary: Lord Nightstitch of the Secret Pillow

lore.common: Buttons itself crookedly every evening and insists it looks fashionable.
lore.uncommon: Hides one slipper inside its sleeve so bedtime becomes a treasure hunt.
lore.rare: Makes any pillow feel as soft as a cloud. The cat has confiscated three.
lore.epic: Sneaked into a castle in the middle of a formal banquet and turned every suit of armour into pyjamas. The knights slept through the invasion drill.
lore.legendary: Lord Nightstitch stitched a blanket from a thousand children's best dreams and wrapped it around the sleepless city. By morning even the clock tower had stopped tossing and turning.

names.legendary: Sarongara, Sail of the Wandering Isles

lore.common: Lets its knot come undone at the exact moment somebody stands to order an ice cream.
lore.uncommon: Can become a skirt, shawl or beach blanket, but always chooses the one most embarrassing in a gust.
lore.rare: Catches the wind so neatly that its wearer glides over hot sand without burning a toe.
lore.epic: Unfurled across the beach and scooped up every sun lounger in a single colourful wave. The crabs declared it the first seaside carnival.
lore.legendary: Sarongara was woven for an island sailor who had lost his sail. Her cloth caught a moonlit breeze and carried his fishing boat home across a sea without waves.

names.legendary: Captain Cannonball, the Tomorrow Diver

lore.common: Hides its drawstring inside the waistband whenever a changing-room queue forms.
lore.uncommon: Dries before the swimmer reaches the towel, then jumps back into the pool out of spite.
lore.rare: Stores tiny bubbles in its pockets to launch a surprise underwater flip.
lore.epic: Inflated into twin blimps during the diving final and floated the whole swim team across the spectator stands.
lore.legendary: Captain Cannonball leapt from a diving board so high that he broke through yesterday's clouds. The splash arrived before the lifeguard's whistle.

names.legendary: Threadrick, the Shirt That Remembered

lore.common: Scratches the neck with its label, then hides the scissors used to remove it.
lore.uncommon: Turns itself inside out inside the washing machine and comes out looking extremely pleased.
lore.rare: Attracts every sauce stain in a ten-metre radius, even when dinner is being served elsewhere.
lore.epic: Unravelled across a festival into a giant cotton serpent, stitching every spectator into one enormous team jersey.
lore.legendary: Threadrick was worn by a thousand travellers and remembers each journey in a different stitch. Unpick its oldest seam and an ancient road appears in the cloth.

names.legendary: Madame Veloura, the Final Bow

lore.common: Stops halfway up and insists the audience enjoys a little suspense.
lore.uncommon: Opens just enough to reveal one actor's shoe before retreating dramatically.
lore.rare: Swallows stage lights to turn an ordinary entrance into a magnificent silhouette.
lore.epic: Dropped across the royal opera during the final aria and refused to rise until the audience applauded the fabric itself.
lore.legendary: Madame Veloura has guarded the threshold between story and reality since the first stage was built. When she falls for the final time, every forgotten character takes one last bow.

names.legendary: Vespervelour, the Sleeping Court

lore.common: Gets stroked against the grain and pulls a disgusted face.
lore.uncommon: Keeps every fingerprint, especially the one left beside the biscuit crumbs.
lore.rare: Drinks light until a crimson curtain looks as deep as a midnight sky.
lore.epic: Draped a ballroom in velvet so soft that dancing guests sank ankle-deep. The orchestra had to perform from a life raft.
lore.legendary: Covered the chairs of a cruel court in enchanted velvet. Every lie made its speaker sink deeper until the throne disappeared beneath the floor.

names.legendary: Aurivelle, the Robe of Remembrance

lore.common: Collects candle wax at every ceremony and calls it decoration.
lore.uncommon: Shimmers under the lamps while quietly tripping over its own hem.
lore.rare: Shows old stories in its embroidered threads when the hall falls silent.
lore.epic: Unrolled its ceremonial train all the way down the cathedral steps. The visiting choir was swept into an unscheduled procession.
lore.legendary: Each golden stitch records a promise made beneath the vaulted roof. When the last keeper forgot the words, the entire robe sang them back.

names.legendary: Merina, Spinner of the First Winter

lore.common: Escapes the knitting basket and leaves fluffy footprints on the carpet.
lore.uncommon: Builds a little nest from discarded fibres and claims it is a luxury apartment.
lore.rare: Wraps a shivering lamb in warm fleece without ever touching a knitting needle.
lore.epic: Empress Ewevana knitted scarves for every mountain peak during an unexpected cold snap. The climbers complained they could no longer tell the summits apart.
lore.legendary: Merina gathered the first sheep's lost fleece after a blizzard and wove it into a blanket for the sleeping valley. At sunrise the snow had melted beneath it, and spring returned early that year.

names.legendary: Glovaria, Sisters of the Last Winter

lore.common: Holds hands all winter and gets separated the moment somebody opens the bus door.
lore.uncommon: One glove always disappears when its owner needs both. The other insists it knows nothing.
lore.rare: Can point at secrets its wearer has not yet spoken aloud. Once pointed at a birthday cake three days early.
lore.epic: Made a thousand snowballs in one afternoon and challenged an entire school to a winter battle. The headteacher surrendered first.
lore.legendary: The Sisters of the Last Winter have never been separated, even when the northern seas froze solid. Their handprints can still be found on the gates of spring.

names.legendary: The Two Warm Sisters of Winterfall

lore.common: Can grip a snowball brilliantly but drops the house key every single time.
lore.uncommon: Hang from one string through a coat, holding hands while their owner thinks they have been lost.
lore.rare: Pack snowballs so perfectly that the snowmen hire them to rebuild missing heads.
lore.epic: Challenged a blizzard to a snowball fight and caught every flake in their woollen palms. The entire street woke up wearing snow forts.
lore.legendary: The Warm Sisters took the hands of a winter giant and knitted warmth into his frozen fingers. Spring returned wherever he touched the ground, though he kept losing one mitten.

names.legendary: The Two That Escaped the Dryer

lore.common: Argues with its identical twin about which one is the left sock. Neither knows.
lore.uncommon: Swaps patterns during the washing cycle and comes out dressed for two different weddings.
lore.rare: Can teleport one sock to any drawer in the world, provided the other is desperately needed.
lore.epic: Liberated every matching sock in the launderette and formed a marching army of pairs. The underwear staged a counter-revolution.
lore.legendary: The twins escaped the first tumble dryer ever built and have spent centuries stealing their replacements. Every missing sock is a new recruit.

names.legendary: Lady Bowella, Binder of Unruly Kingdoms

lore.common: Unties itself the moment someone says how lovely it looks. Very modest, apparently.
lore.uncommon: Grows a tighter knot whenever anyone tries to loosen it. The scissors are losing confidence.
lore.rare: Ties itself to anyone who naps for longer than a minute. Grandad woke gift-wrapped.
lore.epic: Wrapped the entire birthday party into one giant present. The guests could only escape when the birthday child pulled the right ribbon.
lore.legendary: Once tied the wind into a bow and gave it to the spring. Every ribbon in the world still flutters when she says its name.

names.legendary: Lord Silkstrangle, the Eternal Windsor

lore.common: Dangles straight into lunch the instant the soup arrives. It particularly likes tomato.
lore.uncommon: Tightens itself whenever its wearer says a meeting will be short.
lore.rare: Slithers into knots no tailor can undo, then wears the bewildered owner to formal occasions.
lore.epic: Coiled around a corporate summit and tied every executive to the same conference table until they finally agreed on something.
lore.legendary: Lord Silkstrangle was knotted at a coronation three hundred years ago and has never loosened. It now attends royal banquets alone, dragging a perfectly dressed suit behind it.

names.legendary: Stivalora, Empress of the Last Step

lore.common: Pinches ankles every time its zipper closes. Claims it is just checking for weak points.
lore.uncommon: Hops over puddles without touching the ground. Leaves its wearer stranded on the wrong side of the street.
lore.rare: Clicks its heel three times to open a hidden path through any crowd. Unfortunately it also summons curious pigeons.
lore.epic: Marched down the capital's grand boulevard and struck the pavement so hard that every clock began ticking to its footsteps. The parade followed for a week.
lore.legendary: Stivalora takes one step whenever an empire falls. Her bootprints become new roads, and kings spend fortunes trying to learn where she will walk next.

names.legendary: Gildric, Lord of False Authority

lore.common: A tiny enamel gremlin that stabs anyone who forgets to admire its shiny face.
lore.uncommon: Collects jackets instead of badges. Its current owner thinks they have simply lost a lot of jackets.
lore.rare: Whatever title is printed on its chest becomes law until somebody notices the spelling mistake.
lore.epic: Pinned itself to the mayor and declared every pigeon a parking inspector. The fines are payable in breadcrumbs.
lore.legendary: One golden pin turned a goat into headmaster, a broom into prime minister and the school hamster into the only competent official.

names.legendary: Madame En Pointe, Duchess of the Air

lore.common: Escapes its owner's heel whenever the bus arrives. It has never missed its own bus.
lore.uncommon: Forces its wearer to bow after every sneeze. Applause is optional but preferred.
lore.rare: Can dance through a crowded room without disturbing a crumb, then trip on its own ribbon.
lore.epic: Spun a hole through the opera house floor and emerged in the orchestra pit. The violins have demanded hazard pay.
lore.legendary: Once danced across a lake without touching the surface. The swans still practise her steps and refuse to admit she was better.

names.legendary: Duke Fluffington, Emperor of Sundays

lore.common: Trails its belt through every puddle between the bathroom and the kettle.
lore.uncommon: Is so comfortable that all plans for the day evaporate the moment it is tied.
lore.rare: Answers the door looking like a royal adviser. Even the parcel courier bows.
lore.epic: Swelled to fill the entire hallway and declared Monday a national holiday. Nobody was in a hurry to object.
lore.legendary: Once wrapped the god of dawn in its sleeves and persuaded him to sleep in. The world enjoyed its first truly glorious lie-in.

names.legendary: Bucklethor, Binder of the Leaning Tower

lore.common: Tightens one notch after every second helping. Calls it nutritional feedback.
lore.uncommon: Bangs its metal buckle against the chair precisely when the room goes quiet.
lore.rare: Whips around the biscuit tin whenever anyone reaches for the last biscuit. Nobody has challenged its claim.
lore.epic: Uncoiled through the town like a leather serpent and buckled every runaway shopping trolley to its owner.
lore.legendary: Wrapped itself around a leaning tower and pulled it perfectly straight. The builders have been arguing for centuries about how to get it off.

names.legendary: Solaria, Duchess of the Golden Shore

lore.common: Tangles its straps into a sailor's knot the instant it enters a beach bag.
lore.uncommon: Leaves a sun-shaped pale patch on the back after a day of lounging. Calls it heraldry.
lore.rare: Summons a castle of fine sand wherever its wearer leaves a towel. The crabs consider it prime property.
lore.epic: Surfed a wave the height of the lighthouse without losing a ribbon. The beach volleyball team now asks it to coach.
lore.legendary: Her ribbons are woven from the first rays of summer. When Solaria enters the sea, even the tides dress for the occasion.

names.legendary: Sir Brogarius, Chancellor of the Step

lore.common: Squeaks in the silent library aisle just when everyone has finally stopped whispering.
lore.uncommon: Collects dust in its fancy little holes and charges its owner for polishing.
lore.rare: Taps out office secrets with every step. The last doughnut thief has already been exposed.
lore.epic: Marched into the boardroom and made every executive's shoes dance under the table. The company called it a morale initiative.
lore.legendary: Brogarius crossed seven kingdoms without scuffing a single polished toe. Each step sounded like a royal decree, usually ordering more tea.

names.legendary: Capenox, Last Cloak of the Sky Knights

lore.common: Gets caught in the door exactly as its wearer makes a heroic exit. The dramatic pause is mandatory.
lore.uncommon: Flutters majestically indoors where there is no wind. Its wearer is less majestic near furniture.
lore.rare: Grants the courage to rescue cats from branches barely taller than the rescuer.
lore.epic: Unfurled above the capital like a crimson thundercloud. Every citizen struck a heroic pose and the traffic lights exploded in applause.
lore.legendary: Capenox carries the forgotten vows of every hero who ever wore a cloak. It can lift mountains, but insists on swooshing before doing anything useful.

names.legendary: Grandma Loopella, Weaver of Lost Winters

lore.common: Catches on every door handle, slowly donating its sleeves to the architecture.
lore.uncommon: Has elbow patches that confer an instant university professorship. The wearer still cannot do maths.
lore.rare: Knits copies of itself while everyone sleeps. The wardrobe is now more cardigan than wood.
lore.epic: Unravelled at a family reunion and tied three generations together in a woollen net. Nobody left without agreeing on Christmas plans.
lore.legendary: Loopella can knit a winter warm enough to wear and unravel a blizzard with one tug. Her favourite creation remains an ugly Christmas cardigan that nobody dares criticise.

names.legendary: Lord Chelsea, the Unlaced Usurper

lore.common: Requires a heroic tug to put on. Then slips off under the dinner table.
lore.uncommon: Stretches its side panels to fit the entire family's feet. Nobody is happy about this.
lore.rare: Walks out of meetings whenever the conversation turns boring. Its owner must follow in socks.
lore.epic: Strutted through the high street with such swagger that every shop mannequin resigned and joined its entourage.
lore.legendary: Lord Chelsea crossed the seven kingdoms without laces, buckles or permission. His heels click only when someone is about to make a spectacularly bad fashion decision.

names.legendary: Studragon, Champion of the Last Whistle

lore.common: Clacks across kitchen tiles like a tiny horse. The dog thinks it's a challenge.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to leave the changing room until every stud has been polished.
lore.rare: Digs into the pitch so fiercely that its wearer becomes impossible to tackle. Also impossible to move.
lore.epic: Scored from halfway across the field with a stamp that sent turf flying like confetti. The groundskeeper demanded a transfer fee.
lore.legendary: Studragon's golden studs were forged from the nails of the first goalposts. He can outrun any opponent, but still takes off his boots before entering the clubhouse.

names.legendary: Grippoth, Master of the Impossible Hold

lore.common: Squeezes toes into a shape that has never appeared in human anatomy. Calls it performance.
lore.uncommon: Clings to the wardrobe when nobody is watching. The other shoes think it's possessed.
lore.rare: Can grip a wall smoother than a politician's apology. Sometimes forgets the climber is attached.
lore.epic: Scaled a glass skyscraper during rush hour and stopped on the top floor to borrow a cup of tea. The lift has never recovered its dignity.
lore.legendary: Grippoth wears soles cut from the last cliff of an ancient world. Its grip cannot fail, though it has spent three centuries stuck to one particularly interesting stalactite.

names.legendary: Noctivane, Cloak of the Unseen Queen

lore.common: Drags its wet hem through every puddle. It insists the water adds mystery.
lore.uncommon: Swirls around its wearer even indoors, particularly when somebody is trying to eat soup.
lore.rare: Makes its wearer invisible to anyone they owe money. Several debt collectors have begun wearing spectacles.
lore.epic: Unfurled across the royal city and stole every shadow for one glorious evening. The actors of the local theatre declared a crisis.
lore.legendary: Noctivane once concealed a queen from the gaze of a jealous god. It still shelters every secret she carried, and occasionally produces a forgotten royal sandwich.

names.legendary: Klompenstein, Thunderlord of the Polders

lore.common: Clomps down the hallway loudly enough to announce breakfast in the next village.
lore.uncommon: Floats away in puddles whenever its wearer steps out. The ducks call it public transport.
lore.rare: Stomps leaks shut in a canal wall with a single wooden heel. The ducks have started saluting it, which is a first for the ducks.
lore.epic: Stamped once on a cobblestone square and sent a wave through every tulip field in Holland. The flowers bloomed in perfect rows out of fear.
lore.legendary: Klompenstein was carved from the oldest oak beside the sea. His steps held back a flood once, and Dutch folklore credits him with inventing the art of walking loudly on purpose.

names.legendary: Masquerion, Wearer of a Thousand Lives

lore.common: Gets stuck around your shoulders the moment you need the toilet.
lore.uncommon: Turns anyone wearing it into an absolutely terrible pirate. Even actual pirates complain.
lore.rare: Makes its wearer indistinguishable from the guest of honour, including at their own wedding.
lore.epic: Invaded the royal masked ball as fifty identical kings. The genuine monarch was arrested for impersonation.
lore.legendary: Has worn the faces of heroes, villains and gods since the first carnival. Nobody knows what lies beneath the final mask, least of all Masquerion.

names.legendary: Crocothrax, King of Questionable Taste

lore.common: Squeaks across tiles like a duck with a grievance.
lore.uncommon: Keeps tiny pebbles in its holes as a personal rock collection.
lore.rare: Turns up at black-tie events and forces every shoe to question its life choices.
lore.epic: Walked into fashion week wearing fifteen plastic charms. The judges wept, then copied the entire look.
lore.legendary: Banned from every royal ballroom, Crocothrax crossed the ocean on its own floating sole. The kingdom that exiled it now sells replicas at an outrageous markup.

names.legendary: Belladonna, Queen of the Endless Summer

lore.common: Rides up at every wave hello and immediately pretends it didn't.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to attend events with a coat check. Believes jackets are censorship.
lore.rare: Creates its own spotlight on every dance floor, to the irritation of actual lighting technicians.
lore.epic: Danced so fiercely at the festival that the entire stage copied its moves. The speakers requested a day off.
lore.legendary: Stole the summer breeze and stitched it into an outfit no winter could touch. Even the frost king had to admit the look was impressive.

names.legendary: Derbion, Footman of the Midnight Court

lore.common: Comes untied on the first step after someone says those look smart.
lore.uncommon: Takes longer to polish than it does to walk anywhere.
lore.rare: Squeaks the answers during exams, but insists on saying them one question late.
lore.epic: Marched down the palace corridor so loudly that the entire royal council stood up in panic. The king was still in slippers.
lore.legendary: Was crafted for a mysterious gentleman who attended every coronation but never grew old. Derbion remembers each kingdom by the sound of its final footsteps.

names.legendary: Dungarion, Gardener of a Hundred Pockets

lore.common: Snaps one shoulder strap in the middle of every serious conversation.
lore.uncommon: Keeps garden snails in the front pocket. They have formed a tenants' committee.
lore.rare: Produces the exact tool a gardener needs from a pocket that was empty a moment ago.
lore.epic: Dug an entire allotment in one night using tools from its endless pockets. By sunrise the vegetables had elected it chairperson.
lore.legendary: Dungarion carries seeds from gardens that no longer exist. Wherever it plants one, an ancient orchard returns, complete with a bewildered scarecrow.

names.legendary: Senora Alpargata, Queen of the Tides

lore.common: Gets its woven sole wet once and spends the rest of the holiday making swamp noises.
lore.uncommon: Leaves the beach in one shoe. The other insists it is on annual leave.
lore.rare: Unravels a strand of its rope sole to rescue runaway beach balls. Sends an invoice in shells.
lore.epic: Lashed every boat in the harbour into a single knot during a summer festival. The fleet had to sail out together and returned as a very confused island.
lore.legendary: Alpargata tied the first sailor's knot and convinced the tide to stop pulling at it. The sea still sends waves to ask if it may borrow the shoe for the evening.

names.legendary: Polarfluff, Weaver of Winter Sparks

lore.common: Grows tiny bobbles after the first wash and calls them decorations.
lore.uncommon: Zaps the owner's hair into a spectacular halo every time it comes off.
lore.rare: Brings half the hedgerow home after a walk. The dog is jealous of its collection.
lore.epic: Built up so much static on a school trip that the class photo glowed blue. The science teacher has requested the jumper for further study.
lore.legendary: Polarfluff once warmed an icebound mountain hut by collecting sparks from every passing storm. The climbers kept its memory in a crackling patch of wool by the fireplace.

names.legendary: Lord Flapfoot, Voyager of Two Seas

lore.common: Announces every step with a slap loud enough to startle seagulls.
lore.uncommon: Loses a strap exactly halfway between the car and the beach.
lore.rare: Can start a conga line on an empty promenade. Its rhythm is impossible to ignore.
lore.epic: Flew off a foot at the top of the water slide and crossed the pool like a tiny speedboat. The lifeguard presented it with a medal.
lore.legendary: Separated from its twin by a great storm, Flapfoot drifted across two oceans and reunited on a distant beach. The pair now refuse to go anywhere without a spare strap.

names.legendary: Sir Strikewell, Lord of Final Goals

lore.common: Smells like a changing room and insists this is an expensive perfume.
lore.uncommon: Collects half the pitch in its studs. There are rumours it has a fully functioning meadow in the cupboard.
lore.rare: Kicks such wicked curves that the ball asks for motion-sickness tablets.
lore.epic: Hit the winning shot so hard that the stadium scoreboard flipped over and revealed an entirely different sport.
lore.legendary: In the final second of the final match, Strikewell kicked the moon into the top corner. The astronomers still debate whether it was offside.

names.legendary: Madame Lofty, Duchess of the Skyline

lore.common: Gets stuck between cobblestones and announces the problem with a dramatic wobble.
lore.uncommon: Makes every trip to the shops sound like a horse entering a grand ballroom.
lore.rare: Grows its wearer's height with every step. By dessert the party guests are looking up at the chandelier.
lore.epic: Clicked across the palace floor so loudly that every stained-glass window rattled in time. The royal orchestra surrendered the stage.
lore.legendary: Madame Lofty danced above a harbour on heels tall as lighthouses. Sailors followed the glittering shoes home and remembered the dance long after the music stopped.

names.legendary: Solemnis, the Thousand-Mile Wanderer

lore.common: Starts every walk with enthusiasm and ends it with a dramatic little blister.
lore.uncommon: Grips a slippery path so tightly that three clumps of mud arrive home as permanent passengers.
lore.rare: Knows the path home through any forest, but always insists on visiting the scenic waterfall first.
lore.epic: Tramped over a whole mountain range to retrieve one lost sock. The sock declined to explain how it got there.
lore.legendary: Solemnis crossed the ancient paths before roads had names. Each place its sole touched became a safe stepping stone for travellers who came after.

names.legendary: Glissandra, Lady of the Summer Ice

lore.common: Turns its wearer into a baby deer the moment they step on the rink.
lore.uncommon: Cuts elaborate patterns in the ice that look suspiciously like rude drawings of the coach.
lore.rare: Carves a perfect figure eight that keeps spinning after the skater has stopped.
lore.epic: Spun a frozen pond into a whirlpool of glittering ice. A fish surfaced in a tiny scarf to ask for lessons.
lore.legendary: Glissandra glided across the unfrozen lake on midsummer's day, freezing a path with each silver step. The swans still skate her old route at moonrise.

names.legendary: Commander Coverall, Pilot of the Skyfold

lore.common: Needs to be peeled off completely whenever its wearer needs the loo.
lore.uncommon: Zips from ankle to chin and traps one loose scarf in the process.
lore.rare: Sneaks onto anyone standing still and dresses them head to toe before they realise.
lore.epic: Zipped itself so fiercely in an aircraft hangar that it launched its wearer across the runway. The air traffic controller gave it a flight number.
lore.legendary: Coverall learned to fly after its pilot vanished in a storm. It brought the aircraft home alone, landed on a single wheel and hung itself neatly in the locker.

names.legendary: MacSwish, Guardian of the Ancient Plaid

lore.common: Collects thistles in its pleats and delivers them directly to the wearer's chair.
lore.uncommon: Swishes so proudly that everyone hears imaginary bagpipes as it passes.
lore.rare: Changes tartan patterns to match the family dog, much to the clan's confusion.
lore.epic: Spun through the Highland games and sent every caber flying into a neat row of flagpoles. The judges gave it points for landscaping.
lore.legendary: MacSwish carries the tartan of a clan erased from every record but its own. On misty mornings the missing castle appears wherever its pleats touch the heather.

names.legendary: Lady Longstep, Strider of the Deep

lore.common: Requires a five-minute wrestling match just to pull up its zipper.
lore.uncommon: Hugs the leg so tightly that the wearer walks like a very fashionable penguin.
lore.rare: Grows a little taller for every puddle it crosses, until the knees need a map.
lore.epic: Kicked the entire autumn leaf pile into the air during a parade. For a glorious hour, every tree in town had the wrong leaves.
lore.legendary: Lady Longstep walked out into a flooded valley and never broke stride. The waters parted around her boots, leaving a dry road the villagers still use when the river rises.

names.legendary: Cordelius, Warden of the Hidden Floors

lore.common: Swings its badge into your chin every time you sprint for the lift.
lore.uncommon: Gets its clip caught in the desk drawer and holds its owner hostage until lunch.
lore.rare: Unlocks doors it has never seen before, then pretends it only meant to open the supply cupboard.
lore.epic: Opened every secured office floor at once and gave the staff a scavenger hunt through departments they'd never heard of. Payroll found a chocolate fountain.
lore.legendary: Cordelius holds an access pass to the floor between floors. Only at midnight does its lift open, revealing a forgotten office where every lost pen, mug and ambition waits patiently to be reclaimed.

names.legendary: Madame Elastika, Bridge of the Bends

lore.common: Develops a baggy knee just as its owner leaves for a fitness class.
lore.uncommon: Stretches perfectly for every squat, then refuses to let go of the sofa cushion.
lore.rare: Can reach the television remote from the other end of the room without anybody standing up.
lore.epic: Turned a yoga class into a slingshot and sent the instructor sailing across the pond. She landed in the lotus pose.
lore.legendary: Madame Elastika can stretch from one mountain to the next without a single loose stitch. Travellers cross her woven bridge at dawn, and the valleys beneath never hear a footfall.

names.legendary: Vespera, the Golden Face of Midnight

lore.common: Snaps its elastic against the back of the wearer's head and calls that an introduction.
lore.uncommon: Hides its owner's face so well that the family dog demands identification.
lore.rare: Exchanges identities with whoever glances into its painted eyes. The headteacher is still wearing the gardener's moustache.
lore.epic: Confused the entire palace masquerade until the servants went home as dukes and the dukes found jobs washing dishes.
lore.legendary: Vespera arrived at the last masquerade of a vanished kingdom wearing the face of dawn. When her mask fell, the night itself bowed and left the ballroom.

names.legendary: Quietfoot, the Trail Without a Shadow

lore.common: Feels every little stone underfoot and complains about all of them in a whisper.
lore.uncommon: Wears beadwork so beautiful the magpies have appointed themselves its jewel thieves.
lore.rare: Crossed the woods without snapping a twig. The deer offered it a position in forest security.
lore.epic: Walked so silently through the sleeping forest that even falling leaves paused rather than make a noise. The woodcutters thought time had stopped.
lore.legendary: Quietfoot walked a sacred path through the first snowfall without leaving a mark. Those who follow its invisible trail find their way home from any wilderness.

names.legendary: Madame Mulette, the Wandering Heel

lore.common: Falls off a foot at the first opportunity. The other shoe pretends not to know it.
lore.uncommon: Skates across polished tiles with no heel to slow it down, leaving a very confused owner behind.
lore.rare: Escapes beneath café tables and turns up at the next table demanding a croissant.
lore.epic: Tapped across the terrace so loudly that the café chairs joined in. By noon the entire square was doing an accidental dance routine.
lore.legendary: Madame Mulette walked from Paris to the sea without a foot inside her, following the scent of fresh pastries. Every cobbler who met her swore she was looking for her missing heel.

names.legendary: Lady Slumberveil of the Floating Stair

lore.common: Trips over its own hem every time its wearer tries to sneak downstairs for a midnight biscuit.
lore.uncommon: Glides along the landing like a ghost with excellent taste in bedtime fashion.
lore.rare: Glows softly through a dark house, attracting moths that mistake it for a portable moon.
lore.epic: Led a whole neighbourhood of sleepwalkers to the bus stop in their nightclothes. The first bus arrived wearing a dressing gown.
lore.legendary: Slumberveil crossed the sleeping city on a breeze, gathering restless dreams in the folds of her gown. At dawn she returned each dream neatly folded beneath its owner's pillow.

names.legendary: Captain Cosytail of the Pyjama Knights

lore.common: Has animal ears that flop over your eyes the instant the cartoon gets interesting.
lore.uncommon: Hides the zip pull halfway down its own back and calls that a security feature.
lore.rare: Grows soft little paws when the house gets cold. Its owner can no longer hold a mug.
lore.epic: Put an entire sleepover into accidental hibernation. The children woke in spring with perfect hair and several unanswered homework sheets.
lore.legendary: Captain Cosytail defended the Pillow Kingdom through the longest winter, armed with a mug of cocoa and an unbreakable zip. Not one blanket was left uncovered.

names.legendary: Old Stitchbuck of the Hundred Harvests

lore.common: Rattles its buckles whenever the mechanic tries to sneak out early.
lore.uncommon: Has twelve pockets, and each contains exactly the screwdriver nobody was looking for.
lore.rare: Throws mud straight back at the pig that launched it. The pigs now aim at the boots instead.
lore.epic: Hid an entire harvest in its pockets during a hailstorm. The farmer discovered the hay in his trousers after the village dance.
lore.legendary: Old Stitchbuck belonged to seven generations of farmers and remembered where every lost tool lay buried. On the final harvest, his pockets spilled enough seeds to turn a ruined field green again.

names.legendary: Sir Oxford, Keeper of Proper Footsteps

lore.common: Requires polishing before breakfast and sulks at every puddle.
lore.uncommon: Ties its laces in a perfect little bow while its wearer is trying to leave the house.
lore.rare: Walks into interviews so confidently that the questions start answering themselves.
lore.epic: Led a grand ballroom dance without a dancer. The other shoes followed in flawless formation until every guest was barefoot and applauding.
lore.legendary: Sir Oxford walked through the royal court for a hundred years without a single scuff. His final step left a golden footprint that still appears whenever a promise is kept.

names.legendary: Queen Slumberina of the Seven Sundays

lore.common: Pairs a stripy top with spotted trousers and calls it a complete outfit.
lore.uncommon: Lets its elastic go just as its owner starts climbing the stairs.
lore.rare: Makes every ordinary Tuesday feel like a lazy Sunday. The office printer has begun wearing slippers.
lore.epic: Convinced an entire city to hold a pyjama day, including the mayor's official parade. The brass band performed lying down.
lore.legendary: Queen Slumberina stole six exhausting mornings from a kingdom and replaced them with one glorious, endless Sunday. Nobody could explain why the toast always stayed warm.

names.legendary: Parkarius, Bearer of the Northern Flame

lore.common: Has a hood so deep that its wearer waves at the wrong bus stop.
lore.uncommon: Hides three gloves, two biscuits and a mystery receipt in its endless pockets.
lore.rare: Keeps its owner warm during a blizzard so fierce that nearby icicles try to climb inside.
lore.epic: Sheltered an entire school trip beneath its enormous fur-lined hood. The teacher counted thirty heads and one very grateful fox.
lore.legendary: Parkarius carried the last spark of a northern village through the polar night, wrapped against a storm no fire could survive. When he returned, spring followed in his footsteps.

names.legendary: Lady Altissima, Queen Above the Crowd

lore.common: Adds four inches to your height and subtracts all ability to walk down stairs gracefully.
lore.uncommon: Clicks its giant soles to the beat of any nearby music, including the dentist's waiting-room radio.
lore.rare: Leaves sparkling footprints that turn dull pavements into dancefloors for an hour.
lore.epic: Stomped so hard at the midnight disco that the glitter ball fell from the ceiling and kept the party rolling down the street.
lore.legendary: Lady Altissima danced above the heads of a thousand guests at a royal masquerade. Her footsteps became bright stars that still trace the ancient ballroom's outline.

names.legendary: Ponchero, Cloak of the Wandering Herd

lore.common: Turns into a fabric tunnel whenever someone tries to pull it over their head.
lore.uncommon: Keeps its owner's shoulders dry but dumps every raindrop neatly into their boots.
lore.rare: Unfolds into a tiny emergency shelter at the first hint of rain, even while its wearer is on the bus.
lore.epic: Caught a mountain gust and carried its owner sailing over the valley. They landed at the village bakery and ordered lunch.
lore.legendary: Ponchero covered a stranded herd of llamas through the wildest storm in a century. Its bright woven patterns still appear in mountain rainbows after heavy rain.

names.legendary: Downthera, Shield of the Winter Road

lore.common: Makes its wearer look like a startled marshmallow with sleeves.
lore.uncommon: Inflates in the bus queue until three people need to move aside.
lore.rare: Traps a pocket of warm air around anyone caught in a snow squall. It demands payment in biscuits.
lore.epic: Expanded in a ski lift to the size of a small hot-air balloon. The entire queue got a free ride up the mountain.
lore.legendary: Downthera expanded during a blizzard until it sheltered every skier on the mountain. The rescue helicopter landed in its front pocket.

names.legendary: Pumparella, Duchess of the Waltz

lore.common: Pinches its wearer's toe exactly when the music starts.
lore.uncommon: Taps its heel through every waltz, including those played on hold by the dentist.
lore.rare: Leads its owner into a graceful dance with any person or household appliance standing nearby.
lore.epic: Waltzed so fiercely across the ballroom that the chandeliers began revolving in time. The guests danced on the ceiling.
lore.legendary: Pumparella danced in the royal ballroom for one hundred nights without pausing. When the orchestra fainted, the chandeliers took over the rhythm.

names.legendary: Rainwarden, Keeper of the Last Match

lore.common: Its hood blows backward just in time for the first raindrop.
lore.uncommon: Shakes itself dry in the hallway and drenches everybody who was already indoors.
lore.rare: Keeps its wearer warm and dry while the entire street floods ankle deep.
lore.epic: Spread its waterproof sleeves over a crowded market during a storm. The merchants traded beneath it for three days without getting wet.
lore.legendary: Rainwarden sheltered a match meant to light the lighthouse during a storm. The coat arrived so dry that the keeper asked for one in his size.

names.legendary: Ribboria, Weaver of the Festival Sky

lore.common: Tangles itself around the scissors every time someone tries to wrap a gift.
lore.uncommon: Curls itself perfectly on one side and refuses to match the other.
lore.rare: Ties a magical bow that keeps any promise safe until the knot is opened.
lore.epic: Unfurled through the summer fair and bound the whole parade into one gigantic dancing maypole. Nobody could leave before the final song.
lore.legendary: Ribboria wove a ribbon through the clouds to decorate a wedding between two winds. The knot is still causing unexpected breezes each spring.

names.legendary: His Fluffiness, Duke of Dressing Gowns

lore.common: Hangs on the back of the door at night and looks exactly like a sleepy uncle.
lore.uncommon: Has two pockets: one for biscuits and one for secrets. Both are full of biscuit crumbs.
lore.rare: Wraps its wearer in such luxurious warmth that they forget every appointment, including the one with the spa.
lore.epic: Claimed every towel in the hotel as its personal court. The laundry staff now bow before the tumble dryer.
lore.legendary: His Fluffiness defeated a seven-day royal banquet by never getting dressed. By the end the king was wearing slippers and conducting state business from the sofa.

names.legendary: Skidalia, the Shortcut Queen

lore.common: Pretends to be an ordinary shoe until its wearer waves at somebody. Then the floor disappears.
lore.uncommon: Rolls silently past the classroom and makes the teacher question whether walking is still fashionable.
lore.rare: Knows every slope in the shopping centre and chooses the one ending at the chocolate shop.
lore.epic: Glided through the airport at such speed that the moving walkways followed it out of jealousy. The departure boards displayed its name as a flight.
lore.legendary: Skidalia rolled along the world's first rainbow before the paint had dried. Every shortcut since has been a pale imitation of her seven-coloured wheel tracks.

names.legendary: Saunterius, Walker of the Endless Beach

lore.common: Collects sand between its straps and saves it for the car journey home.
lore.uncommon: Insists on being worn with socks during holidays and calls it high fashion.
lore.rare: Leaves a perfect zigzag suntan on its wearer's feet that lasts until Christmas.
lore.epic: Walked along the promenade so loudly that the seagulls fled and the chip sellers rejoiced. Its owner received the key to the seaside town.
lore.legendary: Saunterius has walked the shores of a thousand summers without wearing out his soles. At night, each grain of sand in his straps becomes a tiny memory of the sea.

names.legendary: Sarindra, Weaver of a Thousand Colours

lore.common: Unfolds one perfect pleat the moment the wearer is finally ready to leave.
lore.uncommon: Lets its decorated end trail like a royal banner, then ties a mischievous knot around a chair.
lore.rare: Changes the colours of its silk border to match the wearer's mood. Nobody at the wedding can hide a crush.
lore.epic: Unfurled across the wedding courtyard like a river of embroidered silk. Every guest was swept into the dance, even the caterer carrying soup.
lore.legendary: Sarindra wove the first monsoon rainbow into a length of silk so fine it could pass through a ring. Every time she dances, a forgotten colour returns to the world.

names.legendary: Hornelius, the Giant's Gentle Shoehorn

lore.common: Disappears at the exact moment someone tries to squeeze into their work shoes.
lore.uncommon: Slips a stubborn heel into its boot so smoothly that the wearer suspects witchcraft.
lore.rare: Can fit a giant's foot into an ordinary shoe without stretching the leather one stitch.
lore.epic: Opened a doorway between every shoe shop in the city. Customers emerged in boots they never tried on, waving receipts from other countries.
lore.legendary: Hornelius helped a barefoot mountain giant put on the boots that became two distant hills. Every spring, the giant returns to ask if they need polishing.

names.legendary: Cedragon, the Shoemaker's Immortal Tree

lore.common: Refuses to leave the dress shoe until its wearer offers a very polite apology.
lore.uncommon: Makes a wardrobe smell of cedar and convinces moths to relocate their business.
lore.rare: Restores even the most battered leather shoes to their former shape overnight, though they wake with mysterious footprints.
lore.epic: Sprouted roots inside every shoe in the department store, turning the footwear aisle into a miniature forest. The mannequins demanded gardening leave.
lore.legendary: Cedragon grew from the cedar tree beneath which the first shoemaker worked. His branches carry shoes from every century, and he knows which roads their owners never dared to take.

names.legendary: Lacerion, the Infinite Thread of Travel

lore.common: Comes undone two seconds after someone proudly announces they tied it properly.
lore.uncommon: Tangles into a double knot precisely when the school bus arrives.
lore.rare: Ties together a pair of running shoes so they carry their sleeping owner safely home.
lore.epic: Bound every boot in the marching band together during the parade. They completed the final mile as one extraordinarily musical centipede.
lore.legendary: Lacerion is the lace from the first traveller's shoes, still stretching between the beginning and end of every road. Pull the bow and distant journeys become one step long.

names.legendary: Brrrutus, the Boot That Walked on Winter

lore.common: Clacks across the hotel lobby like a tiny robot wearing pots for shoes.
lore.uncommon: Tightens its buckles after every hot chocolate break. Its owner complains in several languages.
lore.rare: Locks its wearer to the skis on a vertical slope and refuses to let fear undo a single clasp.
lore.epic: Stomped the snow outside the mountain lodge into an enormous staircase. Every beginner climbed to the summit without needing the chairlift.
lore.legendary: Brrrutus has marched through a thousand blizzards without a single cold toe. Where his heavy boots land, the snow settles into solid steps for travellers following behind.

names.legendary: Slumborius, the Warmest Wanderer

lore.common: Disappears under the bed and refuses to come out until both feet are freezing.
lore.uncommon: Sneaks across the kitchen tiles silently, except when it finds the squeaky board.
lore.rare: Walks its sleeping owner back to bed from anywhere in the house without waking them.
lore.epic: Charged itself with carpet static and lit every lamp in the cottage. Grandad declared it the cheapest electricity contract ever.
lore.legendary: Slumborius wandered a hundred frozen winters with a pocket of fire inside each soft sole. Anyone who wears him finds their way home by following the scent of warm toast.

names.legendary: Fjorn, the Last Footprint

lore.common: Clomps through every puddle and brings a tiny snowball home inside its lining.
lore.uncommon: Has a fleece tongue that licks cold toes warm. It also collects lint as rent.
lore.rare: Walks across fresh snow leaving enormous yeti tracks. The actual yeti has filed a complaint about impersonation.
lore.epic: Stomped a blizzard into snow bricks and built a fortress around the ski school. The children refuse to return to class.
lore.legendary: During the winter that erased every road, Fjorn left one trail of warm bootprints across the polar night. The footprints were the size of cottages.

names.legendary: Voltara, She Who Outran the Gun

lore.common: Pokes holes in the hallway carpet and insists they are training marks.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to grip anything except the exact patch of track where its owner just slipped.
lore.rare: Launches its sprinter forward so sharply that the starting gun sounds like an echo.
lore.epic: Raced every runner in the stadium at once and left the track etched with glowing sparks. The finish-line camera needed sunglasses.
lore.legendary: Voltara ran the first race before anyone invented a finish line. She is still waiting for the universe to catch up, one spike planted at the edge of dawn.

names.legendary: Stilettara, Dancer on the Razor Moon

lore.common: Gets trapped between the paving stones and makes its owner perform an unexpected curtsy.
lore.uncommon: Announces its arrival with a click-clack louder than a royal trumpet.
lore.rare: Can balance on a single needle heel atop a moving carriage, without spilling a drop of tea.
lore.epic: Danced across the marble palace so fiercely that the floor became a constellation of tiny heel marks. The astronomers are still naming them.
lore.legendary: Stilettara danced along the slender crescent of the moon without a single slip. Her steps became the silver stars that watch the ballroom after midnight.

names.legendary: Silkathra, Weaver of the Endless Ladder

lore.common: Snags on the first chair it passes and starts an extremely fashionable little ladder.
lore.uncommon: Slides down in public and requires frequent dramatic adjustments behind the coat rack.
lore.rare: Stretches into an invisible cord that can catch falling feathers before they touch the ground.
lore.epic: Escaped from a ballroom to wind around the entire grand staircase, turning its elegant steps into a giant silk slide.
lore.legendary: Silkathra wove a ladder of moonlit silk from the sea to the stars. Only those who have lost something precious can see its first rung.

names.legendary: Sir Snapwell, the Unfallen Gentleman

lore.common: Fires its clip at the exact moment someone bends down to tie a shoe.
lore.uncommon: Holds trousers up so enthusiastically they slowly creep toward the armpits.
lore.rare: Can hoist an entire pair of trousers to the rooftop, even while their owner is still in them.
lore.epic: Launched the mayor across the ballroom during a dramatic bow. He landed upright, and the guests thought it was planned.
lore.legendary: Sir Snapwell held the robes of the last giant king together when the mountain winds tried to strip his court bare. The giant still dresses impeccably.

names.legendary: Lord Splashwick of the Bottomless Lake

lore.common: Leaves a wet silhouette on every park bench and calls it abstract art.
lore.uncommon: Wears a pattern so loud that the lifeguard can spot it from the next beach.
lore.rare: Makes its wearer float like a duck, even when they desperately want to touch the pool floor.
lore.epic: Leapt from the jetty and hurled the lake into the surrounding fields, leaving the fish waiting impatiently in puddles.
lore.legendary: Lord Splashwick dived into a lake without a bottom and resurfaced on the other side of the moon, still wearing his ridiculous tropical print.

names.legendary: Aqualisse, Dancer of the Deep Blue

lore.common: Gets one strap twisted just as the race is about to begin.
lore.uncommon: Fades a different colour after every swim and claims it is a new collection.
lore.rare: Changes colour to match the pool tiles, making its swimmer almost impossible to spot during hide and seek.
lore.epic: Stitched a path through a raging river and reversed its flow long enough for the village children to cross.
lore.legendary: Aqualisse once raced the seven sea currents and won wearing a single thread of silver water. The ocean still leaves her a clear lane at dawn.

names.legendary: Musclara, the Bare-Armed Mountain

lore.common: Hangs in the wardrobe and mocks all the jumpers for having sleeves.
lore.uncommon: Flaps its enormous armholes until the person wearing it looks like a windmill.
lore.rare: Gives even the skinniest arms the shadow of a champion bodybuilder at sunset.
lore.epic: Flexed so fiercely during a beach heatwave that every parasol stood at attention and the seagulls started lifting weights.
lore.legendary: Musclara climbed the mountain with nothing but bare arms and a stubborn smile. The stone giant at its peak was so impressed that he struck a pose which became a new ridge.

names.legendary: Madame Eightlegs of the Silken Court

lore.common: Turns every seam sideways before its wearer reaches the bus stop.
lore.uncommon: Collects balloons through static electricity and arrives at parties with its own floating entourage.
lore.rare: Crawls out of its laundry basket to stitch every ladder back together, but never in the right place.
lore.epic: Stretched across the theatre as a living high wire, then marched the entire ballet troupe into the orchestra pit in perfect formation.
lore.legendary: Madame Eightlegs spun stockings for a giant spider's royal wedding and tailored eight matching legs in one night. The spiders still send her silk every spring.

names.legendary: Sir Tunivar, the Cloth of Many Roles

lore.common: Comes loose at the waist every time its wearer bows.
lore.uncommon: Flaps so loudly in the wind that the herald mistakes it for a flag.
lore.rare: Makes its wearer look like a royal guard, village baker or wandering wizard depending on who needs help.
lore.epic: Dressed an entire classroom as knights, then led a very solemn assault on the cafeteria's last bowl of custard.
lore.legendary: Sir Tunivar was stitched from a banner left behind after a forgotten battle. Whoever wears him becomes exactly the hero a frightened crowd needs, even when the crowd consists entirely of chickens.

names.legendary: Rollneck the Philosopher of Winter

lore.common: Climbs up its wearer's chin whenever they try to eat soup.
lore.uncommon: Scratches exactly the patch of neck that cannot be reached in public.
lore.rare: Keeps its wearer so warm during a blizzard that snowflakes melt before touching their ears.
lore.epic: Wrapped an entire lecture hall in its enormous knitted collar, trapping the professor and students in a heated discussion until spring.
lore.legendary: Rollneck hid a wandering scholar's head through a winter of relentless snow. When the collar finally unfolded, the scholar emerged with the answers to every question and absolutely no idea where his hat had gone.

names.legendary: Pantastrophe, the Briefs of Destiny

lore.common: Snaps its waistband at precisely the wrong moment on a crowded bus.
lore.uncommon: Escapes the laundry basket and hides behind the radiator for a week.
lore.rare: Changes colour with each wash until even the family photographs begin looking suspiciously bright.
lore.epic: Blew off the washing line and draped over the town hall statue, which was promptly renamed the Monument of Modesty.
lore.legendary: Pantastrophe once caught a runaway balloon made from a giant's lost bedsheet. The enchanted waistband stretched across the clouds, becoming the world's first emergency parachute.

names.legendary: Regaliax, the Suit of Earned Stripes

lore.common: Keeps one button crooked no matter how carefully the wearer dresses.
lore.uncommon: Straightens every collar in the room and scolds the houseplants for slouching.
lore.rare: Makes anyone wearing it salute at inappropriate moments, including while opening the fridge.
lore.epic: Marched off to school without its owner, passed every inspection and became head prefect before lunchtime.
lore.legendary: Regaliax has been worn by a thousand humble people who stood up for someone weaker. His badges appear only after genuine courage, and no medal can be bought or polished brighter than one freely earned.

names.legendary: Granny Thermara, the Unfreezable

lore.common: Refuses to admit it is too warm for July.
lore.uncommon: Hides beneath four jumpers, quietly claiming all the credit.
lore.rare: Melts the frost on a car window with one determined hug.
lore.epic: Wrapped a whole family in a single knitted vest during a blizzard. The snowmen outside demanded equal treatment.
lore.legendary: Wove its first stitch from the last ember of an ancient hearth. Explorers still carry a thread of it into the polar night, where it glows like home.

names.legendary: Cortessa, the Seven-League Wedge

lore.common: Leaves crumbs of cork along the hallway like an extremely fashionable snail.
lore.uncommon: Balances on its wedge with the confidence of a circus acrobat.
lore.rare: Floats on water just long enough for its wearer to wonder why they're still dry.
lore.epic: Walked a garden fashion show so majestically that the decking began dancing beneath it. The bridesmaids demanded an encore.
lore.legendary: Crossed seven valleys with a single graceful step of its cork sole. Travellers still search for its footprints, each shaped like a tiny summer sandal.

names.legendary: Pelagion, the Skin of the Sea

lore.common: Needs three people and a great deal of patience to climb out of.
lore.uncommon: Squeaks so loudly while being pulled on that dolphins come to investigate.
lore.rare: Makes the chilliest swimmer feel like a warm-blooded seal beneath the waves.
lore.epic: Dived into a winter surf competition and rode a wave straight through a snowstorm. The seals applauded from the shore, wearing borrowed goggles.
lore.legendary: Was woven from the warmth of a deep-sea vent, allowing its wearer to swim beneath the polar ice to the oldest living coral garden without feeling the cold.

names.legendary: Ventorix, the Coat That Faced the Wind

lore.common: Rustles loudly enough to betray its wearer during hide-and-seek.
lore.uncommon: Fills with a gust of wind and walks its owner backward down the beach.
lore.rare: Keeps its traveller dry on a cliff while everyone else's sandwiches fly away.
lore.epic: Caught a sea gale in its sleeves and lifted the entire hiking club off the path. They landed on the mountain summit just in time for lunch.
lore.legendary: Faced a storm that had torn sails from fleets and roofs from towns. Its battered fabric held firm until the wind itself grew tired and passed by in silence.
